Litteraturbanken
The Swedish Literature Bank

The Swedish Literature Bank is a co-operation between the Swedish Academy, the National Library of Sweden, the Royal Swedish Academy of Letters, History and Antiquities, the Language Bank of the University of Gothenburg, the Swedish Society for Belles Lettres, and the Society of Swedish Literature in Finland.

The Swedish Literature Bank is the website for reliable digital versions of Swedish classics. While publishing canonical works by Swedish authors, The Swedish Literature Bank also focuses on neglected authors and genres, effectively establishing a set of ‘minor classics’ alongside  the canonical works. C.J.L. Almqvist, Selma Lagerlöf, August Strindberg and other classics – as well as a wealth of less renowned yet equally interesting authors, awaiting rediscovery. So far, mainly texts in Swedish are available, but over time, a number of works will be offered in translation as well.

The Swedish Literature Bank offers literary works either as searchable e-text, as facsimiles of the original edition, as pdf files or as epub files – often in more than one format. The texts are available free of charge and the software is developed as open source. 

The website is directed towards the general public and students and teachers at every level, as well as towards scholars. The e-texts, which are also available as epub files for download, are based on printed first editions or on later scholarly editions. They are carefully proof-read. A larger number of texts are offered as facsimile, mostly with embedded ocr which makes them searchable as well, although with a lesser degree of precision. For the common reader, introductions and essays provide fresh perspectives on the classics.

The Swedish Literature Bank thus offers the bulk of Swedish classics in reliable electronic editions. We also offer a number of introductions, tools and useful material for school teachers, and we house the Swedish Dictionary of Translators. Simultaneously, we are devoting more efforts to establishing a very substantial collection of less curated texts which will on the one hand – eventually – contain all Swedish literature as images of the original printed editions, on the other hand will make this material available for ground-breaking approaches within the field of “text mining”. We initiated Digital Humanities in the Nordic Countries (DHN) as a way of creating a productive environment which not only furthers Nordic collaborations but also facilitates international contacts through its connection with the European Association for Digital Humanities (EADH) and Alliance of Digital Humanities Organizations (ADHO). Currently, we form part of Culture Analytics and Text Mining (CATMIN): A Nordic Cooperation which also collaborates closely with American experts.
